section.title: Voice commands & app launcher
section.subtitle: Detect command actions inside your voice dictations to launch applications, open links, compose emails, and manage counters.

launcher.label: Voice command app launcher
launcher.description: Intercept voice dictation to launch apps, open links, compose emails, manage counters, start/stop meetings and screen recordings, and keep your Mac awake (e.g. "tucky stay awake for 2 hours").

prefixRouting.title: Prefix-Based Trigger Routing
prefixRouting.description: Route normal voice dictations to AI only if they start with a trigger word (e.g. "tucky"). Prevents dictation latency!
prefixRouting.toastUpdateFailed: Failed to update prefix routing settings
prefixRouting.phoneticNote: * Note: "tucky" triggers loose phonetic matches (tucky, tuckey, tuckie, tuki) automatically!

actionHotkey.title: Dedicated Action Hotkey
actionHotkey.description: Press a custom key combination to trigger Action Command mode directly. Always runs AI and bypasses prefix rules.

editSelection.title: Edit Selection Hotkey
editSelection.description: Highlight text in any app, hold this hotkey, and speak an instruction (e.g. "make this more concise", "translate to French"). The local model rewrites the selection in place.

counter.title: Automated Actions Count
counter.description: Number of voice actions run successfully

section.title: Voice format templates
section.subtitle: Say "tucky, format as email …" (or use the Action hotkey) to rewrite your dictation with a custom system prompt before it gets pasted.

templates.explainer: When your dictation starts with one of a template's trigger phrases (e.g. <mono>"tucky, format as email …"</mono>), the rest of the sentence is rewritten through the template's system prompt before it's pasted at your cursor. Works with both the "tucky" prefix and the dedicated Action hotkey.
templates.empty: No templates yet. Add one to enable voice formatting.

fields.triggerPhrasesPlaceholder: format as email, make this an email
fields.systemPromptPlaceholder: Describe how the model should rewrite the dictation. Be specific about tone, length, and what to omit.

section.title: Google Drive
section.subtitle: Upload screen recordings to Drive and get an anyone-with-the-link share URL. The app only sees files it creates (scope drive.file).

drive.defaultSharingLabel: Default sharing: anyone with the link can view
drive.sharingNote: Applied to each file (not the folder). Override per video when you upload.
drive.byoClientLabel: Use my own Google OAuth client (removes the unverified-app warning)
drive.howToCreateClientId: How to create a client ID

setupModal.title: Set up your own Google OAuth client
setupModal.step1: Open the <link>Google Cloud Console</link> and create a project (or pick an existing one).
setupModal.step2: APIs & Services → Library → search Google Drive API → Enable.
setupModal.step3: APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen → External → fill in the app name and your email → add the scope .../auth/drive.file → add your Google account under Test users → Save. Leave it in Testing.
setupModal.step4: APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID → Application type: Desktop app → Create.
setupModal.step5: Copy the Client ID and Client secret into the fields below. No redirect URI is needed — Desktop apps allow loopback automatically.
setupModal.secretNote: Stored securely on this Mac. Leave the secret blank when editing to keep the saved one.

toolPermissions.title: Tool permissions
toolPermissions.subtitle: Tucky has a built-in MCP server that agents like Claude Code or Codex can connect to. Tick what they're allowed to access — changes apply immediately, even for agents already connected. Everything stays on this Mac.

connect.title: Connect your coding agent
connect.subtitle: The MCP server is the Tucky app itself — nothing extra to download. Click Install and Tucky registers itself with the agent's own CLI, or copy the snippet to do it by hand.

claudeCode.title: Claude Code
claudeCode.hint: Install runs: claude mcp add (user scope).

other.title: Other MCP clients
other.hint: Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI — standard mcpServers JSON.

howToUse.title: How to use it
howToUse.subtitle: There's no command to memorize — talk to your agent normally. It sees the Tucky tools and calls them whenever your request needs them; mentioning “Tucky” nudges it to look there. Try one of these:
howToUse.recordingNote: For recording prompts, Tucky must be running and the Screen recording permission ticked above. The agent lists your windows, starts and stops the recording itself, gets the video file path back, and can then watch or analyze the file — the recording also lands in your library like any other.

examplePrompts.listWindows: List my windows with Tucky and record the Chrome window with system audio. Stop when I tell you and summarize what happened in the video.
examplePrompts.recordBug: Record my screen with mic on while I reproduce this bug, then stop and analyze the video for what went wrong.
examplePrompts.searchMeetings: Search my Tucky meetings for the pricing discussion and summarize the decisions.
examplePrompts.lastWeekDictation: What did I dictate last week about the onboarding flow?

section.title: Permissions
section.subtitle: Re-grant microphone or accessibility access if something feels broken. Reset & quit clears macOS's TCC grants for both services so the next launch re-prompts cleanly.

section.title: Diagnostics
section.subtitle: Inspect the rolling crash log Tucky writes to your home folder.

resetSection.warning: Wipes the settings store (hotkeys, active models, persisted preferences) and quits the app. Your captured items are preserved — they live in the SQLite database, not the settings store.
resetSection.confirmMessage: Reset onboarding? This clears the settings store and quits the app. You'll need to relaunch.

uninstall.confirmDeleteMessage: Uninstall Tucky and remove all local data? This includes captured items, recordings, downloaded models, settings, logs, the local event archive, and the Google Drive connection. Files will be moved to the Trash, but the Drive credential and macOS permission grants will be removed.
uninstall.confirmKeepMessage: Uninstall Tucky but keep all local data? The app will quit and move to the Trash. Reinstalling later will restore your items, recordings, models, settings, and preferences.

appOnly.title: Uninstall application
appOnly.body: Removes only Tucky. Your captured items, recordings, downloaded models, settings, and preferences stay on this Mac and are available after reinstalling.

appAndData.title: Uninstall application and data
appAndData.body: Removes Tucky and all of its local data, including items, recordings, models, settings, logs, and the local event archive. Use this only when you want the next install to start fresh.

uninstall.trashNote: The application and filesystem data are moved to the macOS Trash.
